aggregators.name: AGG_AVERAGE
aggregators.description: Arithmetic mean of the field across the input set.

aggregators.name: AGG_COUNT
aggregators.description: Count records that pass the active filter, optionally by group.

aggregators.name: AGG_DISTINCT_COUNT
aggregators.description: Count of distinct non-null values across the input set.

aggregators.name: AGG_FREQUENCY
aggregators.description: Per-distinct-value count of the field (returned as map in Details).

aggregators.name: AGG_GEO_BBOX
aggregators.description: Bounding box (min/max lat/lon) of point_f64 values.

aggregators.name: AGG_GEO_CENTROID
aggregators.description: Spherical centroid (lat, lon) of point_f64 values.

aggregators.name: AGG_KURTOSIS
aggregators.description: Bias-corrected excess kurtosis via online moments.

aggregators.name: AGG_MAX
aggregators.description: Largest non-null value of the field.

aggregators.name: AGG_MEDIAN
aggregators.description: 50th percentile of the field; requires sorting the full value set.
aggregators.streamable_hint: Use AGG_AVERAGE for a streaming central-tendency proxy, or accept the buffered path.

aggregators.name: AGG_MIN
aggregators.description: Smallest non-null value of the field.

aggregators.name: AGG_MODE
aggregators.description: Most-frequent value of the field (ties broken by first-seen order).
aggregators.emits_type_note: string (echoes the dictionary value or stringified scalar)

aggregators.name: AGG_PERCENTILE
aggregators.description: Configurable percentile of the field; requires sorting the full value set.

params.name: percentile
params.description: Percentile to compute, in [0, 100]. e.g. 95 for p95.

aggregators.streamable_hint: Use AGG_AVERAGE or accept the buffered path; exact percentiles need sorted input.

aggregators.name: AGG_RANGE
aggregators.description: Spread (max minus min) of the field across the input set.

aggregators.name: AGG_STDDEV
aggregators.description: Population standard deviation via Welford's online algorithm.

aggregators.name: AGG_SUM
aggregators.description: Sum the numeric values of the field across the input set.
aggregators.emits_type_note: scalar float64 (decimal128 preserved when input is decimal)

aggregators.name: AGG_VARIANCE
aggregators.description: Population variance via Welford's online algorithm.

aggregators.name: AGG_ZSCORE
aggregators.streamable_hint: Streaming uses online Welford moments; the ZSCORE aggregate finalize step needs the full deviation sum.

attributes.name: ATTR_DATE_PART
attributes.description: Extract a calendar component (year, month, day, year_month, year_month_day, month_day) from a date field.

params.name: part
params.description: Which calendar component to extract.

attributes.name: ATTR_FORMULA
attributes.description: Per-row expression evaluation against the record's fields (e.g. "price * qty").
attributes.emits_type_note: one float per record (booleans coerce to 0/1)

attributes.name: ATTR_PERCENTILE
attributes.description: Per-row percentile rank against the post-filter value set; requires sorting.
attributes.streamable_hint: Use ATTR_NORMALIZED for a streaming-friendly rank proxy.

attributes.name: ATTR_REG_FITTED
attributes.description: Per-row fitted value ŷᵢ = Xᵢ · β + β₀ from a regression refit during the attribute prepass. Carries its own RegressionSpec-shaped fields (Target, Predictors, Penalty, Alpha, L1Ratio); each ATTR_REG_* attribute refits independently (Option A). Accepts any OLS penalty (unpenalized, ridge, lasso, elasticnet).

attributes.name: ATTR_REG_LEVERAGE
attributes.description: Per-row hat-matrix diagonal hᵢᵢ = 1/n + (xᵢ − μ_x)ᵀ · M2_xx⁻¹ · (xᵢ − μ_x) from an unpenalized OLS refit. Range ∈ [0, 1]; Σᵢ hᵢᵢ = p + 1. Restricted to unpenalized OLS — penalized leverage / GLM leverage deferred.
attributes.streamable_hint: Requires unpenalized OLS only; any non-empty Penalty surfaces PROCESSING_CONFIG.

attributes.name: ATTR_REG_RESIDUAL
attributes.description: Per-row residual yᵢ − ŷᵢ from a regression refit during the attribute prepass. Sums to ≈ 0 when the fit includes an intercept (always true for OLS). Accepts any OLS penalty; reuses the same fit machinery as ATTR_REG_FITTED.

attributes.name: ATTR_TSCORE
attributes.description: Per-row T-score: z-score scaled and shifted to mean 50, stddev 10.

attributes.name: ATTR_ZSCORE
attributes.description: Per-row standardized z-score: (value − mean) / stddev computed via Welford two-pass streaming.
attributes.emits_type_note: one float per record (NaN when stddev=0)

filterers.name: FILTER_EXCLUDE
filterers.description: Drop records whose field value appears in the supplied Values list.

filterers.name: FILTER_EXPRESSION
filterers.description: Keep records for which Expression evaluates truthy; reads any record field.

filterers.name: FILTER_GEO_WITHIN
filterers.description: Keep point_f64 records that lie inside the supplied polygon (Values lists vertices).

filterers.name: FILTER_GEO_WITHIN_RADIUS_M
filterers.description: Keep point_f64 records within radius (m) of a reference point; Values=[lat, lon, radius_m].

filterers.name: FILTER_INCLUDE
filterers.description: Keep records whose field value appears in the supplied Values list.

filterers.name: FILTER_RANGE
filterers.description: Keep records whose numeric field value falls within [low, high]; Values=[low, high].

groupers.name: GROUP_CATEGORY
groupers.description: Partition records by exact field value; ideal for categorical fields.

groupers.name: GROUP_DATE
groupers.description: Partition date-typed records by a calendar component (year, quarter, month, week, day, day_of_week).

params.name: component
params.description: Calendar component to bucket by.

groupers.streamable_hint: Use GROUP_CATEGORY on an ATTR_DATE_PART output column for a streaming-friendly substitute.

groupers.name: GROUP_H3_CELL
groupers.description: Group spatial records by H3 cell at the configured resolution; accepts point_f64 (converts inline) or h3_cell (re-bins via parent walk).

params.name: resolution
params.description: Target H3 resolution in [0, 15]; finer resolutions bucket more aggressively.

groupers.emits_type_note: string H3 cell index per row

groupers.name: GROUP_QUANTILE
groupers.description: Partition records into N equal-population quantile buckets (Q1..Q4 / D1..D10 / P1..P100).

params.name: interval
params.description: Number of buckets. Conventional values 4 (quartiles), 10 (deciles), 100 (percentiles); set on the request's Group.Interval field, not in Params.

groupers.emits_type_note: bucket label per row (Qk / Dk / Pk)
groupers.streamable_hint: Quantile cutoffs need the sorted value set; use GROUP_RANGE or GROUP_ROUNDED with known bounds for streaming.

groupers.name: GROUP_RANGE
groupers.description: Partition numeric records into half-open ranges [a, b); Interval controls the bucket width.

params.name: interval
params.description: Bucket width on the value axis; set on the request's Group.Interval field.

groupers.name: GROUP_ROUNDED
groupers.description: Round each numeric value to the nearest multiple of Interval and group by the rounded scalar.

params.name: interval
params.description: Rounding increment; set on the request's Group.Interval field.

windows.name: WIN_DENSE_RANK
windows.description: Dense rank with no gaps after ties (1, 2, 2, 3, …) within the ordered partition.

windows.name: WIN_EWMA
windows.description: Exponentially weighted moving average; current = α·value + (1−α)·previous.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Smoothing factor in (0, 1]; higher values weight recent observations more.

windows.name: WIN_LAG
windows.description: Return the value of Field from the row N positions before the current row in the ordered partition.

params.name: offset
params.description: Lookback offset (≥ 1).

params.name: default
params.description: Substitute value when the lookback row does not exist.

windows.emits_type_note: one float per row (Default when offset crosses partition start)

windows.name: WIN_LEAD
windows.description: Return the value of Field from the row N positions after the current row in the ordered partition.

params.name: offset
params.description: Lookahead offset (≥ 1).

params.name: default
params.description: Substitute value when the lookahead row does not exist.

windows.name: WIN_MOVING_AVG
windows.description: Moving average of Field over the configured Frame; Frame width must be bounded.
windows.emits_type_note: one float per row (NaN when frame is empty)

windows.name: WIN_PCT_CHANGE
windows.description: Percent change relative to the row Periods positions earlier in the ordered partition.

params.name: periods
params.description: Lookback offset (≥ 1) for the comparison row.

windows.emits_type_note: one float per row (NaN when previous value is zero or missing)

windows.name: WIN_RANK
windows.description: Sparse rank with gaps after ties (1, 2, 2, 4, …) within the ordered partition.

windows.name: WIN_ROW_NUMBER
windows.description: 1-based row index within the ordered partition.
windows.emits_type_note: one integer per row (resets per partition)

windows.name: WIN_RUNNING_AVG
windows.description: Running average of Field over the configured Frame within the ordered partition.

windows.name: WIN_RUNNING_SUM
windows.description: Running total of Field over the configured Frame within the ordered partition.

features.name: FEAT_BUCKETIZE
features.description: Bin a numeric column into ordered buckets using explicit boundaries or N equal-population quantiles.

params.name: boundaries
params.description: Sorted ascending list of bucket cutpoints (mutually exclusive with quantiles).

params.name: quantiles
params.description: Number of equal-population buckets (mutually exclusive with boundaries).

features.emits_type_note: single column "<label>" with bucket index per row

features.name: FEAT_DATE_FEATURES
features.description: Expand a date field into year, month, day, day_of_week, and is_weekend columns.

features.name: FEAT_FREQUENCY_ENCODE
features.description: Replace each categorical value with its observed relative frequency in the cohort.
features.emits_type_note: single column "<label>" with frequency per row

features.name: FEAT_LOG
features.description: Per-row natural log of Field; emits one f64 column.

features.name: FEAT_ONE_HOT
features.description: One-hot encode a categorical field as one f32 column per dictionary entry.
features.emits_type_note: one column per dictionary entry, prefixed by label

features.name: FEAT_POLY
features.description: Per-row polynomial expansion of a numeric field; emits Degree-1 derived columns x_2 .. x_Degree. Pair with REG_OLS to fit polynomial regression.

params.name: degree
params.description: Polynomial degree; must be >= 2 and <= 10. Degree 1 (linear) is the original column.

features.name: FEAT_SQRT
features.description: Per-row square root of Field; emits one f64 column.

features.name: FEAT_TARGET_ENCODE
features.description: Replace each categorical value with the smoothed mean of a numeric Target field for that category.

params.name: target
params.description: Numeric field whose grouped mean is encoded into the output column.

params.name: smoothing
params.description: Bayesian smoothing weight blending category mean with global mean.

features.emits_type_note: single column "<label>"; risk of target leakage on non-CV pipelines

features.name: FEAT_TRAIN_TEST_SPLIT
features.description: Emit a deterministic split assignment column (0=train, 1=val, 2=test) for ML workflows.

params.name: ratios
params.description: Two- or three-element ratio list summing to ~1.0.

params.name: seed
params.description: RNG seed; same seed produces byte-identical assignments.

params.name: stratify
params.description: Optional categorical field; ratios are applied per category for class balance.

features.emits_type_note: single column "<label>" with split assignment per row

tests.name: TEST_ANOVA_F
tests.description: One-way ANOVA F-test comparing Field means across the categorical SplitBy partition.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_ANOVA_RM
tests.description: Repeated-measures one-way ANOVA; rows pivoted on SubjectField × SplitBy condition.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_ANOVA_WELCH
tests.description: Heteroscedasticity-robust one-way ANOVA with Welch-Satterthwaite df correction.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_BROWN_FORSYTHE
tests.description: Homogeneity-of-variance test; one-way ANOVA on absolute deviations from per-group medians.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_CHISQ
tests.description: Chi-square independence test on a 2D Rows×Cols contingency table.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_FISHER_EXACT
tests.description: Exact two-sided p-value for a 2×2 Rows×Cols contingency table; small-sample CHISQ alternative.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_KENDALL_TAU
tests.description: Concordance-based correlation between Field and Field2; buffered O(n²) pair count.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_KRUSKAL_WALLIS
tests.description: Nonparametric k-group location test; ANOVA-like rank sums under tie correction.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_KS
tests.description: Kolmogorov-Smirnov two-sample distribution test on Field partitioned by SplitBy.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

params.name: alternative
params.description: One- or two-sided test.

tests.name: TEST_MANN_WHITNEY_U
tests.description: Nonparametric two-sample location test; buffered tie-corrected rank sum.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_PAIRED_T
tests.description: Paired-sample t-test on the per-row difference d = Field − Field2.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_PEARSON_R
tests.description: Parametric Pearson correlation between Field and Field2; reports r and a t-test p-value.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_PROP_Z
tests.description: Two-proportion z-test on the success rate of Field across two SplitBy groups.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

params.name: success

tests.name: TEST_SHAPIRO_WILK
tests.description: Shapiro-Wilk normality test on Field; runs per-group when SplitBy is set (n ≤ 5000).

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_SPEARMAN_R
tests.description: Rank-based correlation between Field and Field2 (monotonic association).

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_T
tests.description: One-sample or two-sample Welch t-test on a numeric Field; SplitBy switches to the two-sample variant.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

params.name: mu
params.description: Hypothesized mean for the one-sample variant (ignored when SplitBy is set).

tests.name: TEST_WELCH
tests.description: Explicit two-sample Welch t-test alias; identical to TEST_T with SplitBy.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

tests.name: TEST_WILCOXON_SR
tests.description: Wilcoxon signed-rank test on per-row d = Field − Field2; buffered tie-corrected sign-rank sum.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

post_tests.description: Pearson correlation between two output columns of the result row set.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

post_tests.name: TEST_SHAPIRO_WILK/shapiro_francia_post
post_tests.description: Shapiro-Francia normality test on an output column (Shapiro-Wilk variant for the post-row set).

regressions.name: REG_BAYES_LINEAR
regressions.description: Bayesian linear regression with a conjugate Normal-Inverse-Gamma prior; reports posterior means, std errors, and credible intervals.
regressions.emits_type_note: RegressionResult with coefficients (posterior means), std errors, R², adjusted R², residual std error, credible_intervals.
regressions.streamable_hint: Streamable in isolation; setting Resample or Selection on the request forces the buffered path.

params.description: Response variable field name.

params.name: predictors
params.description: Predictor field names (numeric only in v1).

params.name: prior
params.description: Prior family; only the conjugate Normal-Inverse-Gamma is shipped in v1.

params.name: prior_mu
params.description: Prior mean vector for coefficients.

params.name: prior_precision
params.description: Prior precision scalar.

params.name: prior_shape
params.description: Inverse-gamma shape parameter for residual variance.

params.name: prior_rate
params.description: Inverse-gamma rate parameter for residual variance.

params.name: credible_level
params.description: Posterior credible-interval mass.

params.name: resample
params.description: Orthogonal resampling layer.

params.name: bootstrap_iters
params.description: Replicate count when resample == bootstrap.

params.name: rng_seed
params.description: Seed for the bootstrap RNG.

params.name: selection
params.description: Subset-selection wrapper.

params.name: criterion
params.description: Information criterion driving selection.

modifiers.name: selection
modifiers.description: Automated subset-selection wrapper; non-empty forces the buffered path. Requires criterion when set.

regressions.streamable_hint: Always buffered; IRLS requires multiple passes over the data.

params.description: Replicate count when resample == bootstrap.

synth_distributions.name: bernoulli
synth_distributions.description: Bernoulli samples emitting 0 or 1 with probability p.

params.description: Probability of 1 in [0, 1].

synth_distributions.name: constant
synth_distributions.description: Emit a constant value on every row; useful for unit testing and placeholder fields.

synth_distributions.name: exponential

synth_distributions.name: lognormal
synth_distributions.description: Log-normal samples with log-space mu and sigma.

params.name: mu
params.description: Log-space mean.

params.name: sigma
params.description: Log-space standard deviation (> 0).

synth_distributions.name: monotonic_from
synth_distributions.description: Strictly increasing or decreasing integer counter; useful for synthetic primary keys.

params.name: start
params.description: First emitted value.

params.name: step
params.description: Increment per row (non-zero).

synth_distributions.name: normal
synth_distributions.description: Gaussian samples with optional [min, max] clamp.

params.name: mean
params.description: Distribution mean.

params.name: std
params.description: Standard deviation (> 0).

params.name: min
params.description: Optional lower clamp.

params.name: max
params.description: Optional upper clamp.

synth_distributions.name: pareto

params.name: alpha

synth_distributions.name: poisson

synth_distributions.name: weighted_categorical
synth_distributions.description: Discrete categorical samples drawn from values with optional weights.

params.name: values
params.description: List of dictionary values to draw from.

params.name: weights
params.description: Optional weight list matching values length; uniform when absent.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_ask
pulse_compose
mcp_tools.description: Execute a batch of processing requests in one round-trip. Use when you have multiple distinct types.Request payloads to run against the same or different cohorts. For single-question analytical asks, prefer pulse_ask.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_drop
mcp_tools.description: Drop a managed-import handle from the pool, deleting the .pulse file and its sidecar. Errors with PULSE_IMPORT_SOURCE_MISSING when the handle is unknown. Pulse-format passthroughs are unaffected (they were never managed).

mcp_tools.name: pulse_errors_lookup
mcp_tools.description: Look up Pulse error code metadata. Pass code=PULSE_XXX for full detail on one code. Pass domain=PULSE/ENCODING/PROCESSING/SERVICE/DATA/CLI to enumerate that domain. Pass query="text" for keyword search across descriptions and fixups. The manifest carries only the code-name list — fetch detail here on demand to keep session context lean.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_examples_get
mcp_tools.description: Fetch one request example from the embedded library by `name`. Returns the full record including `body`, a runnable types.Request JSON with the _meta annotation block stripped — hand it straight to pulse_process or pulse_predict.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_examples_search
mcp_tools.description: Search the embedded request-example library. Filters: `query` (case-insensitive substring across name, description, and operators), `tags` (ANDed list of canonical taxonomy tags such as `time-series`, `experiment-analysis`, `tier-1-test`), and `category` (exact directory: `aggregations`, `attributes`, `features`, `filterers`, `groupers`, `tests`, `windows`). Returns lightweight summaries (name, category, tags, operators, description); fetch the runnable JSON body via pulse_examples_get.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_facet
mcp_tools.description: Return distinct values for a field in a cohort. Diagnostic / discovery tool — use after pulse_ask when you need the unique-value set of one column (e.g., before authoring a FILTER_INCLUDE).

mcp_tools.name: pulse_import
mcp_tools.description: Import a tabular source file (csv, tsv, ndjson, jsonarray, parquet, arrow, excel) into a managed .pulse handle, or pass through an existing .pulse file unchanged. Auto-detects format from the extension; override via `format`. Managed handles live in $PULSE_DATA_DIR/imports/ with a TTL-tracked sidecar — every subsequent inspect/predict/process/sample/facet/ask against the handle slides expiry forward. TTL accepts Go duration form (`24h`, `30m`, `3600s`, `1h30m`) plus day suffix (`7d`, `30d`) and `pin` for never-expire. Returns the handle, managed path, format, row count, expiry, and a managed flag. Pulse-format sources skip the copy + sidecar; they pass through with managed=false.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_imports_list
mcp_tools.description: List every managed-import handle currently in the pool with its sidecar metadata: source path, source format, imported_at, expires_at, ttl, expired flag, pinned flag. Sweep is not invoked — expired entries are flagged via Expired so callers can render them and decide whether to drop or extend.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_inspect
mcp_tools.description: ADVANCED. Read header and schema of a .pulse file. Never reads record data. Typically callers should use pulse_ask instead — pulse_ask runs inspect + predict + execute in one call and is the preferred entry point for analytical questions. Use pulse_inspect directly only when you need schema-only output without running a request (e.g., listing fields for a UI, debugging dictionary contents).

mcp_tools.name: pulse_manifest
mcp_tools.description: Return the root Pulse manifest — the LLM-authored-request bootstrap blob. Carries per-operator params + accepted field types + streamability, tier-1 + tier-2 test catalogs as peer slices, synth distributions, error codes, MCP tool list, and cohort field types with operator cross-references. Call once at session start, cache the result, reference it for every subsequent request authoring decision. MCP always returns the slim payload (no prose descriptions); fetch operator prose via pulse_skills_get when needed.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_predict
mcp_tools.description: ADVANCED. Validate a processing request against a cohort schema without executing. Typically callers should use pulse_ask with predict=true instead — same validation, plus auto-import and natural-language query support, in one call. Use pulse_predict directly only when you need standalone validation diagnostics on a pre-built request (e.g., a request constructor verifying its output before storage).

mcp_tools.name: pulse_process
mcp_tools.description: ADVANCED. Execute a pre-built processing request against an existing cohort. Typically callers should use pulse_ask instead — pulse_ask accepts a `source` path (auto-imports), a `query` (natural language), and produces the same execution result plus structured fixup suggestions on failure. Use pulse_process directly only when you already have a hand-authored types.Request and a cohort handle, AND want to skip the inspect + predict round-trip.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_sample
mcp_tools.description: Return up to N rows from a cohort. Diagnostic / preview tool — use after pulse_ask if you want to eyeball the underlying data.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_skills_get
mcp_tools.description: Fetch the markdown body of a named skill.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_skills_list
mcp_tools.description: List available embedded skills with their descriptions.

skills.name: aggregation-guide
skills.description: Choose between the 18 AGG_* operators (SUM, AVG, MEDIAN, PERCENTILE, ZSCORE, FREQUENCY, MODE, KURTOSIS, GEO_CENTROID, GEO_BBOX, ...) and 6 FILTER_* operators. Use when assembling a Process request, interpreting percentile/frequency output, or picking a row-filter.

skills.name: attribute-composition
skills.description: Compose ATTR_FORMULA, ATTR_ZSCORE, ATTR_TSCORE, ATTR_NORMALIZED, ATTR_PERCENTILE, ATTR_DATE_PART rows for derived columns. Use when adding computed fields, normalizing values, or chaining attributes inside a request.

skills.name: cohort-schema-design
skills.description: Pick the right .pulse field type — u8/u16/u32/u64, f32/f64, decimal128, categorical_u8/u16/u32, nullable_*, packed_bool, date, point_f64, h3_cell. Use when designing a schema, evaluating storage layout, or choosing nullability and bit-packing tradeoffs.

skills.name: compose-requests
skills.description: Run several Process requests against one cohort in a single pulse_compose call — order-preserving slot-by-index, optional parallel execution. Use when comparing operator outputs, fan-out reporting, or batching multiple analyses for one MCP round-trip.

skills.name: contributor-workflow
skills.description: Step-by-step recipes for extending Pulse — adding aggregators, attributes, filterers, groupers, windows, features, statistical tests, synth distributions, I/O formats, MCP tools, error codes, field types. Also covers porting, debugging predict mismatches, regenerating goldens, wiring an MCP client, and running CI gates locally. Use when modifying Pulse internals.

skills.name: debugging-with-predict
skills.description: Validate a request against a .pulse schema with pulse_predict before executing — surfaces field-name typos, type mismatches, leakage warnings, streamability gates, and applied defaults. Use when a Process call errored or before running an expensive request.

skills.name: error-code-reference
skills.description: Read Pulse error envelopes (DOMAIN_CATEGORY codes across CLI/DATA/ENCODING/PROCESSING/PULSE/SERVICE) and call pulse_errors_lookup for per-code Message + Fixup detail. Use when a tool call returns errors[] or warnings[] you don't recognize.

skills.name: export-format-selection
skills.description: Pick the right export format — CSV (universal), TSV, NDJSON, JSON array, Parquet (columnar analytics), Arrow IPC (zero-copy handoff), Excel (humans). Use when wiring Process output into a downstream tool or warehouse.

skills.name: feature-engineering
skills.description: Apply pre-filter FEAT_* operators — FEAT_LOG, FEAT_SQRT, FEAT_BUCKETIZE, FEAT_ONE_HOT, FEAT_FREQUENCY_ENCODE, FEAT_TARGET_ENCODE, FEAT_DATE_FEATURES, FEAT_TRAIN_TEST_SPLIT — for ML pipelines. Use when preparing training data; covers the target-leakage trap and PULSE_FEAT_TARGET_LEAKAGE_RISK.

skills.name: financial-cohorts
skills.description: Use decimal128 / nullable_decimal128 for money — precision and scale propagation, banker's rounding, divide-by-zero policy, currency-column patterns. Use when a cohort has monetary fields or hits PULSE_DECIMAL_OVERFLOW / PRECISION_LOSS / DIVIDE_BY_ZERO errors.

skills.name: geospatial-cohorts
skills.description: Use point_f64 and h3_cell for spatial data — AGG_GEO_CENTROID, AGG_GEO_BBOX, FILTER_GEO_WITHIN, FILTER_GEO_WITHIN_RADIUS_M (meters), GROUP_H3_CELL resolutions, antimeridian behavior, polygon WKT format. Use when a cohort has lat/lon or H3 fields or hits PULSE_GEO_* errors.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Pulse mental model, MCP tool surface, .pulse file format, operator vocabulary. Use first on a new session to establish baseline before calling pulse_inspect, pulse_predict, or pulse_process.

skills.name: grouper-design
skills.description: Pick a grouper: GROUP_CATEGORY, GROUP_DATE (day/week/month/year/quarter), GROUP_RANGE (intervals), GROUP_ROUNDED, GROUP_QUANTILE, GROUP_H3_CELL. Use when bucketing rows, nesting groupers for cross-tabs, or choosing between range and quantile bins.

skills.name: import-best-practices
skills.description: Import CSV, TSV, NDJSON, JSON array, Parquet, Arrow IPC, or Excel into .pulse with safe schema inference, null markers, fail-closed semantics. Use when building a new cohort or troubleshooting PULSE_IMPORT_* errors like CATEGORICAL_OVERFLOW or SCHEMA_AMBIGUOUS.

skills.name: mcp-integration
skills.description: Pulse's MCP tool surface (pulse_manifest, pulse_inspect, pulse_predict, pulse_process, pulse_ask, pulse_compose, pulse_sample, pulse_facet, pulse_examples_search/get, pulse_errors_lookup, pulse_synth_*), pulse:// and pulse-skill:// resources, schema-bound field enums on inspect, recommended session bootstrap order.

skills.name: query-router-prompt
skills.description: System-prompt template a calling LLM uses to translate natural-language analytical questions into a Pulse AskRequest JSON payload. Use when wiring Pulse behind an upstream LLM (Nexus, agent shells) that takes free-text user input and must route to pulse_ask.

skills.name: regression-modeling
skills.description: Fit OLS (with optional l1/l2/elasticnet penalty), GLM (logistic, poisson, gamma), and Bayesian linear regression. Use when a request needs coefficient estimates, R²/deviance, std errors, or per-row residuals; covers the 13 textbook regression names (Simple/Multiple/Linear/Logistic/Ridge/Lasso/Polynomial/Bayesian/Jackknife/ElasticNet/Ecological/Stepwise) via 3 operators + 2 modifiers + FEAT_POLY composition.

skills.name: request-recipes
skills.description: Canonical Pulse request JSON skeletons keyed by analytical intent — compare two groups, rank top N, trend over time, ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc, paired before/after, frequency cross-tab, geo aggregation. Use when starting from a natural-language ask and needing a runnable JSON template.

skills.name: statistical-testing
skills.description: Run tier-1 row tests (TEST_T, TEST_WELCH, TEST_CHISQ, TEST_ANOVA_F, TEST_ANOVA_WELCH, TEST_ANOVA_RM, TEST_KS, TEST_PAIRED_T, TEST_PROP_Z, TEST_PEARSON_R, TEST_SPEARMAN_R, TEST_KENDALL_TAU, TEST_MANN_WHITNEY_U, TEST_WILCOXON_SR, TEST_KRUSKAL_WALLIS, TEST_BROWN_FORSYTHE, TEST_FISHER_EXACT, TEST_SHAPIRO_WILK) and tier-2 post-tests (TEST_TUKEY_HSD, TEST_TREND, variants). Use when a request mentions hypothesis testing, p-values, ANOVA, t-tests, correlations, normality, or post-hoc comparisons.

skills.name: synthetic-data
skills.description: Generate deterministic synthetic .pulse cohorts via pulse_synth_from_schema or pulse_synth_from_profile — 12 distributions (normal, lognormal, poisson, exponential, pareto, bernoulli, weighted_categorical, regex, uniform, uniform_date, monotonic_from, constant), pairwise correlations, constraints. Use when seeding tests or sharing reproducible data without leaking real values.

skills.name: window-operations
skills.description: Apply WIN_LAG, WIN_LEAD, WIN_RANK, WIN_DENSE_RANK, WIN_ROW_NUMBER, WIN_MOVING_AVG, WIN_RUNNING_SUM, WIN_RUNNING_AVG, WIN_EWMA, WIN_PCT_CHANGE — partitioning, ordering, and frame semantics. Use when computing row-relative metrics, time-series transforms, or top-N within partition.
